messages:
Rina: heads up 1: planning thread for next week's launch webinar + battlecard refresh. primary ask: crisp claims + bench artifacts + simple routing for leads. target launch: Wed next week.

Owen: timeline check 1: what do we need by Tue EOD?

Rina: Tue EOD = final claim bullets + bench screenshots + 1-page battlecard draft. Wed AM = email + landing page live.

Priya: for claims, recommend 4 bullets max: predictable cost, tail latency SLOs, managed rollout + fallbacks, private deployment parity. each bullet needs a one-line proof and where the proof lives (bench, case study, doc).

Marco: i'll run an A/B of two headline frames for the post: (A) "Bench: Keeping LLM latency predictable at scale" vs (B) "How to avoid inference bill shock". which resonates more?

Tess: B has click appeal for finance stakeholders, A is better for eng. recommend use B for subject line, A as hero title on the blog.

Owen: benchmark ask: can we show both latency (95th) and cost per 1k tokens under reserved vs burst? need the test harness details for legal.

Priya: yes. run with seq len 256 and 512, mixed chat workload, synthetic concurrency curve, and model variants: high-acc float32 and quantized 8-bit. include batch settings and caching enabled/disabled.

Marco: i'll capture the graphs. plan: single figure with latency on y-axis, request rate on x-axis, and color-coded vendor lines. another small table for cost comparisons.

Rina: battlecard structure for SDRs: competitor at top, 3 short pain points, our counterclaim (20 words), proof artifact (link). keep each card to half a page.

Owen: competitor list to cover: major cloud AI, top 2 public LLM APIs, and two inference infra products. Priya: add specific friction points per competitor?

Priya: yes. example: CloudX -> "multi-tenant tail latency"; LLMAPI -> "opaque pricing & hidden egress"; InfraCo -> "operational overhead & slow rollouts".

Tess: objection handlers (short): Q: "Why not maintain my own infra?" A: "Redwood reduces ops burden with rollout tooling + SLO-backed capacity options; frees engineers to productize features."

LegalBot: reminder: avoid absolute negatives like "never" or naming competitors as incapable. include methods appendix and link to raw data. I'll need 48 hours to review claims + bench.

InfraBot: routing plan deployed to staging: form fields = intent, company_size, tokens_est. sample rule: if intent contains "pilot" and company_size > 500 -> AE-enterprise; if tokens_est > 250000 -> SDR-dedicated; if compliance_flag == true -> solutions-eng.

Owen: for webinar CTAs: 1) Download bench PDF (gated) 2) Request a pilot 3) Join the private demo. map to routing rules.

Marco: landing page copy drafts: hero, 3 proof bullets, quick explainer of reserved vs burst pricing, CTA. will drop copy here by EOD.

Priya: will prepare bench methods text and a short JSON schema for the appendix with fields we must publish: model_name, seq_len, batching, concurrency, cache_enabled, raw_latency_samples_url.

Rina: owners: Marco = landing + visuals; Priya = bench + appendix; Owen = battlecard + routing mapping; Tess = copy + email lines; LegalBot = legal review.

Tess: email subject candidates: "Avoid inference bill shock: live benchmark + playbook" OR "Predictable LLM latency at scale 1 webinar". leaning first for broader appeal.

Owen: SDR one-pager will include top 4 objections + short rebuttals and a triage funnel to identify AE-ready accounts. I'll sketch that tomorrow.

Marco: quick ask 1: can design reuse the purple benchmark palette we used in Q1? keeps continuity.

Rina: yes. also keep the benchmark appendix downloadable as JSON + human-friendly PDF. Legal needs the JSON link.

LegalBot: once final claims and appendix are in, tag me and i'll prioritize review. avoid cross-vendor hashtag comparisons.

InfraBot: deployment note: form -> internal router -> slack-alert to #leads-inbound when AE-enterprise routes fire. scheduled for Wed 09:00 UTC.

Rina: ok everyone, please drop your final copy into this thread by Tue 18:00. we'll do a dry run Wed 08:30. thanks! :rocket:
